doc.title: Barry Harris — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Charlie Parker, dances and house parties
title: Big band theaters and being mistaken for Hen Gates
summary: Every city had a theater for big bands; people thought Harris played with Dizzy's band but it was James Foreman.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: No, there was a theater for big bands in every city, almost. You know, you gotta think about it. Every city had it – don’t think that New York had the Apollo, and that was the only – no, no. Detroit had the Paradise, Washington had the Howard, I think it was the Howard. ‘Cause Cannonball – we played opposite um – who did we play opposite? Ray Charles at the Howard. We played opposite Ray Charles at the Apollo and never went to the Howard Theatre in Washington. I think it was the Howard. Chicago had the Regal, or something like that. Yeah, the Regal. Yeah so every place had a theater where big bands came. Big bands were strong. And um, I had people accuse me of playing with Dizzy’s big band. But what they saw was this kid who had a head like mine, yeah that’s right. But his name was Hen Gates.

Hen Gates. And it really was James Foreman, Philadelphia pianist, you know. He looks a lot like me, you know. Maybe a bit taller. And people thought I was Playing with Diz, but I wasn’t, you know. So, come to the ‘60s with Cannonball, I stayed with them maybe for the same amount of time I stayed with Max, maybe about three months, yeah.
[To somebody else in the room] I think he just come. Hey, come on in here.
